note: THE join-trap table, per language. Rev 1 shipped one conflated '*' footnote across six languages; two of the locally-testable cells were wrong (Node path.join and Ruby File.join do NOT reset) and Rust was omitted entirely (Path::join REPLACES on absolute).

verified.what: join → /base/etc/passwd; resolve → /etc/passwd. The reset primitive in Node is resolve, not join (rev-1 error).

php.primitive: naive '.' concat; realpath() collapses but does not reset

verified.what: concat keeps prefix; realpath('/base/../etc/passwd') == '/etc' (collapses dotdot, does not 'reset')

verified.source: .NET docs: 'If path2 contains an absolute path, this function returns path2'

java.primitive: Path.resolve (resets) / Paths.get (does not clean or reset)

verified.source: java.nio.file.Path docs: resolve returns the absolute argument

go.primitive: filepath.Join — joins and Cleans, does not reset

verified.source: Go path/filepath docs (Join semantics: Clean of concatenated elements)

rust.primitive: PathBuf::push / Path::join — an absolute argument REPLACES the buffer

verified.source: Rust std docs: 'if path is absolute, it replaces the current path'

hazards: the correct guard is resolve-then-prefix-check (assert resolved starts with base+sep) — checking the RAW input before decoding is bypassable
Windows adds ..\ and drive-absolute forms; test both separators
a reset-primitive language (python/dotnet/java-resolve/rust) means an absolute input needs NO dotdot at all
non_transfers: object stores with opaque keys (no filesystem semantics)
